summary: This component renders a blog post card in two different layouts—small and big. It accepts a post object with metadata like title, date, and tags, then displays them in a styled card format. The component uses Docusaurus utilities for localization and slug generation, and applies different JSX structures and CSS classes depending on which layout is requested.

explanations.13: This interface defines the shape of a blog post object, including optional fields like description, date, and tags that might not always be present.
explanations.20: The description field accepts undefined, null, or a string because different parts of the codebase might pass null explicitly to hide the description even if it exists.
explanations.29: The layout prop has only two valid values: 'big' for the full-featured card or 'small' for a compact version.
explanations.36: The default assignment means if the caller doesn't pass a layout, it will default to 'big'.
explanations.40: This destructures the post object so we can use its properties directly (like 'title' instead of 'post.title').
explanations.41: useDocusaurusContext is a Docusaurus hook that gives us access to site-wide context, including the current language locale.
explanations.42: This formats the date string into a readable format using the current language, so dates display correctly for different locales.
explanations.50: This uses the post's image if it exists, otherwise falls back to a default placeholder image.
explanations.60: This renders the counter element only if the post actually has a counter value.
explanations.87: createSlug converts the tag name into a URL-safe format (like 'My Tag' becomes 'my-tag') so it can be used in the URL path.
explanations.90: getTagLabel retrieves the display name for a tag, which might be different from its internal identifier.
explanations.102: This conditionally renders the description only if it exists and isn't null, preventing empty elements from appearing.
explanations.110: Math.ceil rounds the reading time up to the nearest whole number so we don't show fractional minutes like '4.3 min read'.
